review_basis:
Seventh golden authored from the project's own newly-expanded real corpus, this time via a genuinely new discovery METHOD: a single large automated scan run unattended across 20 previously-untouched files from BOTH GitHub Release archives in one pass (survey each file's sheets for a detected scale and a segment count safely below the pathology threshold Runs 24-25 established, time a single center-point trace on each qualifying sheet as a live pathology guard before committing to a full sweep, then grid-sweep only the sheets that pass). This one scan found real hits across SEVERAL files at once (SDSU, St. Louis VA, MSU Reid Hall, Orange County, and others) -- a real step up in throughput over Runs 22-27's own one-sheet-at-a-time method.

A real, explicitly REJECTED candidate from this SAME scan is worth disclosing plainly, not silently dropped: `05_MO_VA_StLouis_AHU_VAV_Replacement` sheet MH204 produced a 33.70 LF `30x36 RA` duct with a genuine, correct automatic bind (`size-binding:leader`, matching a real printed '30x36 RA' callout exactly) -- but a marked render crop showed the ENTIRE surrounding area covered by a large red-hatched overlay explicitly labeled 'NOT IN SCOPE' in bold red text. The duct itself is real, correctly labeled, and correctly read by the engine -- but a real estimator looking at this drawing would never take it off, since the drawing itself explicitly excludes this area from the renovation contract's own scope of work. Using it as a golden would validate a technically-correct engine read that no real takeoff would ever include. A new, disclosable category distinct from Runs 25's legend-sample and Run 26's civil-annotation-leader false positives: a real, in-scope-looking duct that the drawing's own explicit scope annotation excludes.

The candidate actually used (this golden): a real 36x20 EA (exhaust air) duct riser on SDSU's own Engineering Sciences Complex schematic-design mechanical sheet, confirmed via a marked render crop as a real, dash-fragmented (13 real dash-gap bridges) duct running from a real branch point in a private-office ceiling space, through two real 90-degree elbows, down into a real mechanical shaft -- directly beside this sheet's own printed '36x20 EA UP' / '36x20 EA UP/DN' leader-arrow callouts (both labels visible in the same crop, confirming the size/system read). No 'NOT IN SCOPE' overlay or other scope-exclusion marking appears anywhere near this run.
scope: A single real 36x20 exhaust-air (EA) duct riser segment (10.45 LF) on SDSU's own Engineering Sciences Complex 100% schematic-design mechanical sheet M-201N, from a real branch point in a private-office ceiling space, through two real 90-degree elbows, to a real dead end at the mechanical shaft this run's own printed 'UP/DN' callout identifies as a riser continuing further (the continuation itself, both up and down past this run's own two dead ends, is out of scope). Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the REJECTED 'NOT IN SCOPE'-overlay candidate on a different file described in review_basis; the mechanical shaft's own other equipment, flues, and HWR/HWS piping visible in the same crop; every other duct/pipe run on this large, real, multi-part 157-page schematic-design set (only sheet 28/M-201N of part03 sampled); every other file discovered promising in this same large automated scan but not yet authored into a golden.

runs.description: 36x20 exhaust-air (EA) duct riser, from a real branch point in a private-office ceiling space, through two real 90-degree elbows, to a real dead end at a mechanical shaft (the riser's own printed 'UP/DN' callout marks the real continuation beyond this run's own scope).
